then.text: Shrows. Final answer. To all friends round the Wrekin!

else.text: How do I say it? SHROWS-bury, like my grandad, and he could see it from up here on a clear day. Tell them that.
To all friends round the Wrekin! That's the old Shropshire toast. Raise your flask.

They say a giant meant to dam the Severn and drown Shrewsbury with a spadeful of earth. He met a cobbler carrying a sack of worn-out shoes, who said he'd walked so far from Shrewsbury he'd worn them all through. The giant gave up and dropped his earth here. That's the Wrekin.

ib_guide.text: Three Abraham Darbys, grandfather, son and grandson, and every one of them a Quaker ironmaster. Darby the first worked out coke smelting; Darby the third cast the bridge.
Coalbrookdale also cast the first iron rails and some of the first iron steam engine cylinders. If it was heavy and hot, it probably started here.

ib_lamplighter.text: Evening! It's gas, you see. I go round with my pole and light every lamp in Blists Hill. Electric light is a fad, mark my words.
A penny for the sweet shop goes a long way in eighteen-ninety-something. Get a quarter of humbugs and a sherbet dab.

ib_tarman.text: Put the hard hat on. Down there the walls weep tar, real natural bitumen, and they've been weeping since 1786.
They bottled it as British Oil and sold it for rheumatism. Did it work? Well, it smelt as if it should.

ib_housman.text: On Wenlock Edge the wood's in trouble; his forest fleece the Wrekin heaves. A. E. Housman. He wasn't from Shropshire, you know. He just loved it from a distance, like a lot of us.
Pick up any stone up here and look closely. Corals, shells, sea lilies. This hill was a tropical reef, 425 million years ago. I find it a great comfort on a wet Tuesday.

ib_kayaker.text: Ironbridge was famous for its coracles. The last of the old coracle makers here kept going into his nineties. Every family on the river had one hanging on the wall.
Watch the Severn in a spate. It comes up the gorge brown and fast and has been known to visit the pubs.

then.text: Our Olympian! Come back in July. Bring your laurel.
Enter the Wenlock Olympian Games? Four events, no rest between.
Competitors to the Linden Field! On your marks...
All four events! Dr Brookes would have had the band out. Here: a Wenlock medal, as near as we can make it, and a crown of laurel which I'm keeping because it's the only one.

else.text: No hurry. The Games have waited since 1850; they'll wait for you.

then.text: Pop into Much Wenlock Museum first and learn the events. The curator will tell you all about Dr Brookes.

else.text: Welcome to the Linden Field, home of the Wenlock Olympian Games since 1850. Running, jumping, quoits, tilting at the ring, and a great deal of cake.
We're a competitor short for this year's creature pentathlon. Would you have a go? See the curator at the museum first, so you know what you're in for.

g3_coracle_racer.text: A coracle has no keel and no opinions about where you want to go. It only wants to be round. Eight gates down the river, under the bridge, and try not to spin.
